title: Political Science Academic Job Market
text:
1.1 Methodology
The data pipeline has three stages:

PDF Extraction — pdftools::pdf_text() reads raw text from each monthly issue.
Page 2 TOC Parsing — A regex pipeline targeting (N listings) strings on the Table of Contents page extracts the official, ground-truth count per subfield per issue.
Body Text Scraping — The parser walks the document line-by-line, tracking section headers to assign subfields, then flushes a job record each time it detects an eJobs ID: marker.

title: Political Science Academic Job Market
text:
1.2 Verification Report
Scraped record counts are compared to TOC counts for each issue × subfield combination. Rows flagged UNDER indicate the body-text parser missed some listings (usually due to formatting anomalies in older PDFs).


Show Code
verify %>%
  filter(status != "OK") %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(diff))) %>%
  select(source_file, subfield, toc_count, scraped_count, diff, status) %>%
  datatable(
    caption   = "Discrepancies: Scraped Count vs TOC Count",
    filter    = "top",
    options   = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE),
    rownames  = FALSE
  ) %>%
  formatStyle("status",
    backgroundColor = styleEqual(c("UNDER","OVER"), c("#fff3cd","#f8d7da")))

text:
6.2 TF-IDF: Distinctive Terms by Subfield

TF-IDF (Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency) identifies words that are unusually common in one subfield relative to all others — revealing the distinctive vocabulary of each field.



Show Code
tidy_words %>%
  filter(!is.na(subfield)) %>%
  count(subfield, word) %>%
  bind_tf_idf(word, subfield, n) %>%
  group_by(subfield) %>%
  slice_max(tf_idf, n = 8) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(word = reorder_within(word, tf_idf, subfield)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = tf_idf, y = word, fill = subfield)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ subfield, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  scale_y_reordered() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Paired") +
  labs(title    = "Most Distinctive Terms by Subfield (TF-IDF)",
       subtitle = "Words uniquely associated with each subfield",
       x = "TF-IDF Score", y = NULL) +
  theme(strip.text   = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 8))

text:
6.4 Top Bigrams


Show Code
jobs %>%
  unnest_tokens(bigram, full_text, token = "ngrams", n = 2) %>%
  separate(bigram, into = c("w1","w2"), sep = " ") %>%
  filter(!w1%in% stop_words$word, !w2%in% stop_words$word,
         !w1%in% ps_stopwords$word, !w2%in% ps_stopwords$word,
         str_length(w1) > 2, str_length(w2) > 2,
         !str_detect(w1,"^\\d+$"), !str_detect(w2,"^\\d+$")) %>%
  unite(bigram, w1, w2, sep = " ") %>%
  count(bigram, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 25) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = reorder(bigram, n), fill = n)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C", direction = -1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(title    = "Top 25 Bigrams in Job Listings",
       subtitle = "Common two-word phrases after stopword removal",
       x = "Frequency", y = NULL)
